div.p: Only after fsync returns is the write durable. With interval, you may lose up to that window on power loss — that is a documented product decision, not an accident. Redis ships the same tradeoff.
Crash after step 4, before step 6 → the record is on disk. Replay re-applies it. The client never got an ack, so a retry is idempotent (duplicate id is a no-op today).
Crash before step 4 completes → torn tail record. CRC fails on recovery, the log truncates there, the write simply never happened. Both outcomes are consistent.
registry lookup; create or load the collection if cold
monotonic LSN — orders the WAL and marks where a snapshot ends
always — safe, ~1–10 ms/write on consumer NVMe interval — group commit, default ~50 ms never — tests and benchmarks only
Copies so the graph never aliases a caller buffer. Normalizes for Cosine, collapsing it to 1 - dot(a,b).
int(-log(rand) * ml), ml = 1/ln(M) Seeded → replay reproduces the graph
